data.name: Kittu
data.gender_notes: Kittu is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Kittu is derived from the Hindi word 'kitab' which means 'book'. It is often used as a nickname or term of endearment for a little boy or a cub. In Hindu mythology, the god Hanuman is also referred to as 'Kittu' due to his devotion and strength. This name is rich in symbolism, representing wisdom, devotion, and strength.
data.etymology: Kittu belongs to the Hindi linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Little one, cub.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Kittu total 9, giving a life-path number of 9. Number 9 is linked with Mars and with the qualities of compassion, idealism and generosity.

data.cultural_impact: The name Kittu was a popular nickname or term of endearment in North Indian and Nepali communities. It is also the name of a famous fictional character in North-Indian folklore, Kittu the monkey prince of Bharat.
data.spiritual_significance: In Hindu spirituality, Kittu is an alternate name for the revered God Hanuman. Hanuman, an avatar of Lord Shiva, is the embodiment of devotion, strength and selfless service. The name Kittu signifies an embodiment of wisdom and strength, with Hanuman's legacy as a symbol of untiring devotion to Lord Rama.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Kittu is a name derived from the Sanskrit word "Kitti," which symbolizes playfulness and mischief. It is a name given to the child who brings joy and laughter into the family, spreading happiness and cheerfulness with their antics.

historical_references.reference: In the 13th century CE, a Chola king named Kadambur Vengudi Maran Singan II is believed to have ruled over the region of Kittur in Karnataka, India. His name is sometimes referred to as 'Kittu' in local folklore.

In the 18th century CE, a ruler named Rani Chennamma is known to have led the resistance against the British East India Company in the region of Kittur, in present-day Karnataka, India. She is also known by the name 'Kittur Chennamma' and is revered as a heroine in local history.
